correctness.rationale: Hub degree 2t forces >=t paths because a graph-simple path uses at most two hub spokes. Pair one spoke from each of two different cycles and split the remaining internal path of every cycle at a chosen vertex, yielding t paths. In an equality decomposition each path must use two spokes and visit hub exactly once; pairing both spokes from the same cycle would create an impossible simple path on that cycle (branches meet/repeat), hence forbidden. For each petal the two paths adjacent to its spokes must cover the hub-deleted internal path by two disjoint endpoint prefixes: exactly one of ell_i−1 cut vertices, uniquely recoverable. Thus bijection, not merely lower bound. Inclusion–exclusion on t forbidden matching pairs proves D_t sum and recurrence. Independently enumerated all simple paths and exact t-path edge partitions for seven bouquets (2- and 3-petal, lengths up to 5), obtaining 8,12,18,16,64,96,144, agreeing with formula; all-parameter proof is bijective, not empirical. t=1 boundary handled separately.
residual_risks: Finite diagnostics are supporting and do not substitute for infinite/general argument.

final_claim: For a bouquet of t>=2 simple cycles lengths ell_i>=3 sharing just one hub, the minimum number of edge-disjoint graph-simple undirected paths partitioning all edges equals t, and every optimum is uniquely a perfect matching of 2t hub spokes with no same-cycle matched pair plus one of ell_i−1 internal cut vertices in each cycle. Total N(G)=prod_i(ell_i−1) times sum_{j=0}^t (-1)^j binom(t,j)(2t−2j−1)!!, with single-cycle boundary p=2,N=binom(ell,2).
